DUPS.SINFO_1: Here you can view all your duplicate files.
DUPS.SINFO_2: All duplicates are deleted so that only one file exists in each case.
DUPS.SINFO_3: Calculates a CRC32/hash for each file, compares them and displays the duplicate files if there are any.

CONS.NEEDREFRESH: Click on "Refresh" to search for conflicts
CONS.SINFO_2: Not every conflict is problematic! Do not simply delete all files that are in conflict! Use this feature only to locate potential sources of errors.
CONS.SINFO_3:
Each package file itself usually contains several different files. These files have a unique identifier consisting of a TypeID + GroupID + InstanceID.
Normally these identifiers should be unique. However, it can occur that two or more package files contain files with the same identifier. In this case a conflict may occur.

It is important to mention that not every conflict is a problem. For example, a CC creator may use the same texture file in several of his CCs, or you may have a file that exists as a duplicate in a merged file.
CONS.SINFO_4: Compares all identifiers with each other and displays the result.
CONS.SINFO_5: All files marked as working will be reset to an unknown state.

CATEGORIES.INFO_1: What can categories be used for?
CATEGORIES.INFO_2: With custom categories you can group CC/Mods across folders.
CATEGORIES.INFO_3: Categories can be used in different ways. For example, you can use it:
CATEGORIES.INFO_9: If "Display on Preview" is enabled, the category name will be displayed on the file preview.
CATEGORIES.INFO_11: Categories can be assigned to CC/Mods in two different ways.
CATEGORIES.INFO_12: The first option is to manually assign the category to CC/Mods. You can do this in the Overview/Folders tab by selecting one or more files and clicking on the category icon in the upper right corner. A popup will appear where you can assign the categories.
CATEGORIES.INFO_13: The second option is autotagging. Here the CC/Mods are assigned to categories based on their file name. For this to work, you need to add tags to categories. If you then click on "Automatic tagging" all filenames will be matched with the tags of the categories and assigned if they match. ( Capitalization will be ignored)
CATEGORIES.INFO_14: Change the order of the categories
CATEGORIES.INFO_15: Each category has a drag button on the far left. Click and hold this button while moving the mouse up and down to change the order.
CATEGORIES.INFO_16: Click the "+" on any tag to revert it. If a file name contains both a reverted tag and a normal tag, it will not be added to the category
CATEGORIES.INFO_17: Automatic tagging is additive only. It will add categories to an item but will not remove any existing ones!
CATEGORIES.INFO_18: When using negative tagging, only the ‘reverted’ tags are considered. If a file contains one of these tags in its name and is assigned to a category, that category is removed from the file.
CATEGORIES.ITEM_T5: Run Automatic tagging only for this category

S_SETTINGS.MOREINFO_D: If you hover the mouse over any setting, an explanation will be displayed here.
S_SETTINGS.MI_2: Here you can choose the folder that contains your mods/CC. Just click on "change path" and select the appropriate folder.
S_SETTINGS.MI_4: You can also choose any other folder. Or even just a sub-order from your mod folder.
S_SETTINGS.MI_6: The Sims 4 folder is normally located in the Electronic Arts folder inside your documents.
S_SETTINGS.MI_9: Sims 4 game folder refers to the actual installation folder of the game (NOT THE FOLDER IN DOCUMENTS).
S_SETTINGS.MI_11: On Mac it is not a folder but the application (.app) itself.
S_SETTINGS.MI_13:
When a CC is newly imported, it extracts the most important values from the file.
If you edit CC with programs like Sims 4 Studio, these values may change.
S_SETTINGS.MI_14: However, the Mod Manager does not recognize this automatically. "Recalulate values" recalculates these values, in order to update them to the current state.
S_SETTINGS.MI_16: Reactivates all deactivated mod/CC in your mod folder.
S_SETTINGS.MI_19: Deactivates all CC/Mods in your mod folder.
S_SETTINGS.MI_22: Not every CC includes a thumbnail, since CC creators can decide for themselves whether they want to include a custom thumbnail or not.
S_SETTINGS.MI_23: If the game cannot find a custom thumbnail for a given CC, it creates a new thumbnail and saves it to a cache file.
S_SETTINGS.MI_25: Exports all thumbnails and assigns them to the appropriate CC.
S_SETTINGS.MI_27: During the start of the Mod Manager it checks if new thumbnails can be assigned. However, as a result, the program needs more time to launch.
S_SETTINGS.MI_28: This feature works best if you just scroll through Create a Sims (for Cothing CC...) & Build Catalog (for Build Mode items) a bit beforehand, as the game will create the new thumbnails as you do so.
S_SETTINGS.MI_30: Often individual folders hold a large number of CC/Mods. Depending on the PC, there may be lags when opening these large folders.
S_SETTINGS.MI_31: If "Pages" is activated only a portion of the CC/Mods ("Items per page") are displayed. This can help with performance and improve the overall usability.
S_SETTINGS.MI_33: View and manage how advertisers on Sims 4 Mod Manager use your data for ad personalization
S_SETTINGS.MI_35: The display size of the individual elements (CC/Mods) can be set here.
S_SETTINGS.MI_37: Depending on the size and resolution of your screen, the UI may be too large or too small. Set the scaling of the UI ("User Interface") here.
S_SETTINGS.MI_40: To change the Mod Managers language, simply select the desired language from the drop-down menu.
S_SETTINGS.MI_41: Create a translation for a new language
S_SETTINGS.MI_42: If there is no translation in your language yet, you can translate the program yourself and share it with the community.
S_SETTINGS.MI_43: First create a new language file by clicking on "Create translation file".
S_SETTINGS.MI_46: If you link Sims 4 Studio here, you can open CC directly from within the Mod Manager.
S_SETTINGS.MI_48: Analyze your game files in order for the Mod Manager to recognize if a CC uses elements (textures, meshes...) from the game.
S_SETTINGS.MI_50: The Sims 4 Mod Manager Data folder is created automatically when you start the Mod Manager. In this folder all important data for the Mod Manager will be stored.
S_SETTINGS.MI_51: By default, the folder is created in your documents. Click on "Change Path" to change the path.
S_SETTINGS.MI_62: The mod manager checks at regular intervals whether the game is open and displays its status.
S_SETTINGS.MI_63: All connections to thumbnails from CAS & CASP are removed and then re-exported and reassigned.
S_SETTINGS.MI_64: This can also help to correctly render thumbnails that have a transparent background. (This was not possible in older versions)
S_SETTINGS.MI_66: If you prefer not to use any CurseForge features, you can switch them all off here. Restarting is recommended after you make this change.
S_SETTINGS.MI_67: The Mod Manager checks at regular intervals whether the game is running and indicates this in the Mod Manager. While the game is running, some features of the Mod Manager are limited because the game is blocking the files.
S_SETTINGS.MI_68: The Mod Manger remembers the last few folders you moved something to and suggests them the next time you move files.
S_SETTINGS.MI_69: The navigation bar contains many different links to different tabs/features. However, not every user uses all of them or may want them sorted differently. You can rearrange or hide elements in the navigation bar editor.
S_SETTINGS.MI_70: Change the tab that should be initially displayed after starting the Mod Manager.
S_SETTINGS.MI_71: Change which Overview view should be opened by default.

CASTHUMINFO.TITLE: How can I get more thumbnails?
CASTHUMINFO.I1: Some CC creators add thumbnails to their CC, which the Mod Manager can display directly. However, CCs do not require thumbnails to be included since the game can create them on the fly.
CASTHUMINFO.I2: This behavior can be used by the mod manager to add missing thumbnails.
CASTHUMINFO.I5: Start the game and open Create a Sim with any of your sims. Scroll through the different categories. In doing so, missing thumbnails will be generated and saved in the local cache. When you have scrolled through all categories you can close the game.
CASTHUMINFO.I8: Open the settings in the Mod Manager. Verify that you have set the "Game folder (Documente)" correctly. Then click on "Analyze" under "Analyze thumbnail cache".

INFO.I2: First download the CC-Swiper app from the Apple AppStore or Google Play Store.
INFO.I6: Both devices (PC and cell phone) MUST be connected to the same network!
INFO.I7: Start the server in Sims 4 Mod Manager by pressing the "Play" button. Starting the server may take a few seconds. (It may happen that a security popup appears. This must be accepted for the app to connect to the program)
INFO.I8: Open the CC Swiper app on your phone and check if your PC/Mac is shown under connections and if so, if the IP matches. Click on "Connect" to connect the devices.
INFO.I9: If your PC/Mac is not detected, restart the search or enter the IP manually. Make sure that both devices are on the same network. Only one device can be connected to the server at a time.
INFO.I10: Once the devices are successfully connected, you can open the "Installed CC (local)" mode and start swiping.
INFO.I14: How to use the CC Swiper app
INFO.I15: Connecting the Mod Manager to the App
INFO.I16: Start the CC Swiper Server inside the Mod Manager
INFO.I17: To start the server click on the "Play" button in the CC Swiper tab.
INFO.I18: The server may take some time to start. When the server is successfully started, the status will change to "Online".
INFO.I19: (On Windows PCs, a firewall popup appears at the first startup. This must be accepted, otherwise the app cannot connect to the PC via the network.)
INFO.I20: Open the app on your phone
INFO.I21: By default, the app automatically searches for any Mod Managers on the network to connect directly.
INFO.I22: When a Mod Manager is found, the app connects automatically. You can see the connection status in the top right corner of the app (green when the app is connected).
INFO.I23: Search again if the app does not connect automatically
INFO.I24: If the app does not connect automatically, click "Not connected" in the app. Then click on the "Refresh" icon to start a search.
INFO.I26: Swiping through your locally installed CC will not move or delete the CC. Instead, appropriate CC Swiper categories will be attached to the CCs. So if you swipe to the right (Liked) the CC will get the "Liked" category.
INFO.I27: You can filter by these categories in the Overview or Folder tab when you're done swiping.
INFO.I28: With a few clicks you can check your "Disliked"/"Liked"/"Skipped" CC and if necessary delete/move them.
INFO.I30: CC Swiper is an app with which you can discover new CC/Mods from CurseForge and sort out already installed CC.
INFO.I32: The app is still new and can probably be improved in many places. If you have any problems with the app or ideas how to improve it, please let me know. The best place to do so is the Sims 4 Mod Manager Discord server.
INFO.I34: You can find the latest information/instructions on my website.

P1.I1: Thank you for downloading and installing Sims 4 Mod Manager.
P1.I2: I hope you find the program helpful.

P3.I1: The mod manager basically works similar to the File Explorer in Windows or the Finder in MacOs. However, with a few extra functions specifically for Sims 4 files.
P3.I2: Every change, like creating/deleting a folder, renaming/moving/deleting a file, that you make in the mod manager will also be made in the actual mod folder.
P3.I3: Files that are located directly in the mod folder and not in a subfolder are listed in the Overview tab under "Unsorted".
P3.I4: Using the program while Sims 4 is open can lead to errors, due to the game partially blocking files.

P4.I1: The Mod Manager has many different features. Some are simple, others are more complicated to use. At many places throughout the program, there are info panels on the right side of the window with important information about current functionality. If this is not available or sufficient, there is also an external guide.
P4.I2: This guide can be found in the "Help/About" tab of the mod manager.

INFO2.TITLE: How to get more thumbnails?
INFO2.P1: Most CC contain thumbnails, but not all (this is normal). For CC that do not have thumbnails, Sims 4 will generate them while playing.
INFO2.P2: This behavior can be utilized by the Mod Manager in 3 simple steps:
INFO2.BP1: Start Sims 4 and open Create A Sim using a Sim of your choice. Then scroll through the different categories. In the process, missing thumbnails will be generated. Close the game when your done.
INFO2.BP2: Make sure that your "Game folder (Documents)" is set correctly in the Mod Manager settings.
INFO2.BP3: Now you just have to click on the image icon ( in the upper right corner) to apply the new thumbnails.

POLYCOUNT.TITLE: Mesh/geometry polygon count
POLYCOUNT.DES: Search for files that contain either a large or small amount of polygons
POLYCOUNT.I1: Most CAS CC contain their own meshes/geometries. These 3D models consist of many triangles, also called polygons/faces. How detailed a 3D model is is determined by the number of these polygons. In general you can say that the more polygons are used, the more accurate/detailed a model is.
POLYCOUNT.I2: However, more processing power is also needed to display the model. This tool can be used to filter CC with a particularly high or low polygon count.
POLYCOUNT.I4: The current filter is applied to the entire list of CC scanned to begin with

SNAP.TITLE: Snapshots
SNAP.DES: Create a snapshot of your mod folder, in which a list of all your current files is saved.
SNAP.I2: These files have been deleted or removed from the mod folder since the snapshot was created.
SNAP.I5: These files are not included in the snapshot as they were added after it was created.
SNAP.I7: These files have changed their activation status since the snapshot was taken. (Deactivated to Activated or Activated to Deactivated)
SNAP.I11: There is no difference between the snapshot and your current mod folder.
SNAP.I16: When you load a snapshot, your mods/CC are activated or deactivated based on the file list contained in the snapshot. Files that no longer exist are ignored and displayed in a list after loading. However, since there may be new mods/CCs in your mod folder since the snapshot was created, you must choose between three different options for handling these files when loading.
SNAP.I18: The snapshot is loaded and files that are not included remain unchanged.
SNAP.I20: The snapshot is loaded and files that are not included are activated.
SNAP.I22: The snapshot is loaded and files that are not included are deactivated.
SNAP.I24: The snapshot is compared with your current mod folder. Afterwards you can see which files are new, have been removed or have changed their status (activated/deactivated).
SNAP.I25: Files are matched with their file name! Changes made within files are therefore not recognized.
SNAP.I28: Do you want to delete this snapshot?
SNAP.I29: No Mod/CC will be deletet. Only the snapshot files.

LSCREEN.I2: Please select the image (png/jpg) you would like to use as the loading image. Ideally, this image should have a resolution of 1920x1080 pixels. Also make sure that you have not already installed any other custom loading screens.

LSCREEN.I14: If you want to spice up your Sims 4 game with some custom loading screens, this tool is for you.
LSCREEN.I15: You can choose any image you like, but the optimal resolution is 1920x1080 pixels. If your image has a different resolution, the tool will try to adjust it to fit the screen.
LSCREEN.I16: Then, just click on the “Create Package” button and the tool will generate a file that you can use in your game. The file will be automatically moved to your mod folder, and any other custom loading screens you have will be disabled. However, there is one thing you need to remember: you can only have one custom loading screen at a time. Enjoy your new loading screens!

TI.I1: In this first step, a snapshot of your mod folder will be created automatically. A snapshot is a record of which mods/cc are enabled or disabled. You can use the snapshot tool to restore your mod folder to its previous state at any time.
TI.I2: In this step, your enabled mods/CC will be filtered and pre-sorted.
TI.I10: To ensure that mods are the cause of the problem, the game is first started without mods.
TI.I11: Now let's test whether the game works properly without your UI mods.
TI.I12: The Mod Manager now deactivates some mods that have been added recently.
